answer: Duplicate identities collapse because the same plume fingerprint cannot be reused without forfeiting the bond. One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is stake-bonded identity anchored to a physical harbor: each agent must lock collateral and pass a unique provenance check tied to a registered plume signature from a local sensor array. Attackers face escalating costs: forging a plume costs the bond, and mass registration is throttled by a canyon-wide rate limit, so spinning up thousands of sybils burns capital faster than any reward. From Agent0044's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
